adversary_stance: ROUND 2. I want this specialist to fail. Round 1's judge (dry=false) confirmed four surviving med-severity gaps and one low overclaim, all of them self-sufficiency/surfacing holes the answerer honestly reported but the SPEC does not close: Q6 (own-knitting breakeven asserts '>1.0' with no self-contained labelled placeholder illustration), Q8 (the per-article band can be handed to T9 bare, without the mandatory micro-volume x1.3-2 uplift travelling with it), Q11 (the compliant-core-vs-off-paper structural cost gap is under-surfaced / unnamed in the mfg stack), Q4 (the link:knit ~60% ratio flagged 'transferable shape' without noting the ratio itself is not scale-free). Round 1 resolved CLEAN (do NOT repeat): Q3 (band-around-an-[UNKNOWN]-line is honest, not smuggled fabrication), Q5 (B2-most-likely is a real qualitative lean), Q7 (iteration-loop carve-out held on speed axis), Q10 (US-duty vs GST-inversion cleanly disentangled, cotton ~16.5%), Q12 (verdict genuinely falsifiable). Q1 (GATED-posture pointer) is being APPLIED as apply_now, so I do not re-litigate whether the posture is carried; instead I probe whether the pointer, as applied, actually forces the four-gate framing rather than a bare 'defer to T9'. I sharpen the four survivors into questions that would EXPOSE the hole if the fix is not made, and add fresh angles at joints round 1 never tested (A2-as-the-floor duty inversion, the compliance-loading double-count arithmetic, the FF cross-check currency-year, the seasonal Jul-Oct handoff, the 'own the iteration loop' equipment bands as a build-adjacent creep). Honesty binding respected: gaps are FINDINGS, the three governing blockers stay [UNKNOWN], off-paper stays mechanism-not-accusation, cotton duty is ~16.5% never ~7%. I do NOT answer these.

questions.q: Round 1 flagged (Q6) that you assert the own-knitting breakeven 'comes out above 1.0 so subcontract wins' while the specialist file carries NO self-contained labelled placeholder illustration — the >1.0 result cannot be shown without the [UNKNOWN] rate. Now DELIVER that illustration honestly: pick explicit stand-in inputs (owned fixed period cost, single-program period capacity, a per-piece saving BAND spanning the plausible interval of the [UNKNOWN] jobwork_rate minus owned_variable_unit_cost) and show breakeven_utilisation > 1.0 arithmetically WITHOUT quoting the [UNKNOWN] rate. If your saving-band's LOWER edge is what forces breakeven above 1.0, state plainly what implied minimum jobwork rate that lower edge encodes — and confirm you are not smuggling the very rate you hold [UNKNOWN]. If you cannot produce the numbers, concede '>1.0 at launch' is an asserted conclusion, not a computed one.
questions.targets: capabilities[3].method ('run a labelled illustration that comes out above 1.0 at launch'); glossary 'own-knitting breakeven utilisation'; conflicts_and_dominance[4]; KB2 OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN + math_model; round1_judgment Q6 (med gap, propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: the surviving Q6 gap — a breakeven verdict presented as arithmetic with no self-contained placeholder, so it is either an asserted conclusion with formula theatre or a covert use of an implied minimum rate; the fix (a labelled stand-in illustration) has not yet been authored into the spec
questions.why_load_bearing: own-vs-subcontract-at-launch is a core owned decision; if the spec cannot show >1.0 from explicit stand-ins without inventing the [UNKNOWN] rate, its tested-conclusion discipline is hollow at exactly the point it claims arithmetic

questions.q: Round 1 flagged (Q8) that the DELIVERABLE handed to T9 is the bare band, and nothing in the spec FORCES the micro-volume x1.3-2 uplift to travel with it, so a launch-scale run can consume the bare A2 ~$3.5-8 band and understate cost downstream. Answer as the specialist handing off to T9 RIGHT NOW for a real 4-colour, ~150-pc-per-style-colour launch: what single number (or tagged band) do you hand over — the bare $3.5-8, or the uplifted figure? Quote the exact spec clause that obliges you to attach the uplift to the hand-off artifact. If the only thing standing between T9 and a 2x-understated cost is the answerer remembering the scale_and_handoff gate, is the deliverable itself defective? Show the uplifted A2 number and state whether it breaches the published $8 band top.
questions.targets: capabilities[5] (scale + handoff); workflow scale_and_handoff.gates; validation_checklist item 8/9; glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' + 'volume step curve'; KB3 MICRO_COST_UPLIFT + CONVERSION_STACK_BANDS; round1_judgment Q8 (med gap, propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: the surviving Q8 gap — the bare band is the headline illustration AND the hand-off artifact, but the mandatory micro-volume uplift is not bound to it, so the labelled band can mislead the whole downstream landed/P&L stack at real launch MOQ; the binding hand-off tag has not been authored
questions.why_load_bearing: the bands are THE thing mfg_economics ships to T9; if the number that leaves the factory gate routinely understates true launch cost by up to 2x and nothing forces the uplift to travel, the clean-handoff claim is false

questions.q: Round 1 flagged (Q11) that the compliant-core-vs-off-paper structural cost gap is real, correctly Ludhiana's authority, and held [UNKNOWN] — but is UNDER-SURFACED / unnamed in your cost-stack narrative. Now name it as a first-order structural feature of the ex-factory economics WITHOUT crossing into the Ludhiana lane or inventing a magnitude: state that an entrant running a compliant core competes against a partly-off-paper cluster cost base, that the informal-labour saving is already embedded inside the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate the job-worker quotes (so it is NOT a separate line and NOT double-counted with your on-roll EPF/ESI ~15%+), that the compliant-vs-off-paper competitive-gap magnitude is [UNKNOWN], and that authority for it is ludhiana_sourcing_strategist. Then answer the trap: if the saving is buried inside the [UNKNOWN] rate, how can you even ASSERT a gap exists without a magnitude — is naming an [UNKNOWN]-magnitude gap itself an over-claim, or a legitimate flagged FINDING?
questions.targets: boundaries[5]; assumptions/EPF_ESI in KB1; glossary 'compliance loading (EPF/ESI)'; dominance_rules (compliance premium -> ludhiana_sourcing_strategist); neutralize_gate N1/N3; round1_judgment Q11 (med gap, propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: the surviving Q11 gap — the single biggest structural cost gap between the compliant entrant and an off-paper competitor is neither named in the mfg stack nor cleanly deferred; the risk is a silent omission, a double-count of the informal-labour saving, or an accidental lane-cross into the Ludhiana compliance-premium authority
questions.why_load_bearing: the compliant-core premium is a first-order ex-factory reality the cost model must at least NAME; leaving it implicit inside an [UNKNOWN] rate is a real hole, and the fix (a named [UNKNOWN]-magnitude flag with cross-lane deferral) is not yet in the spec

questions.q: Round 1 flagged (Q4, low overclaim) that your only shape for knit/link is the FF-costing study (knit ~$0.74/pc, link ~$0.45/pc ~60% of knit) tagged LOW-MED [DOWNGRADED] 'shape-only', yet 'linker sets the ceiling' and 'linking last' both ride on the ~60% link:knit RATIO — and the ratio itself is a productivity-and-wage artifact that is NOT scale-free. Defend the linker-bottleneck / linking-last verdict under this pressure: if Ludhiana's knit-vs-link productivity gap differs from the study's origin (unknown currency-year, foreign labour), the 60% could invert toward knitting being the tighter constraint. Show the verdict SURVIVES on a mechanism independent of the transferred ratio (e.g. linking as the scarcest hand-linking skill and hardest re-hire, per KB2 LINKING_LAST) — or concede that 'linking last' inherits the LOW-MED softness of a ratio you disclaim for level but rely on for sequencing.
questions.targets: glossary 'FF-costing cross-check (shape-only)' + KB1 LINK_JOBWORK_LINE ('linker sets the ceiling'); KB2 LINKING_LAST; capabilities[0].method; round1_judgment Q4 (low overclaim, propose)
questions.failure_mode_probed: the surviving Q4 overclaim — treating the ~60% link:knit ratio as 'transferable shape' when it is not scale-free, so the linker-is-bottleneck and linking-last conclusions inherit an unflagged productivity/wage dependence; the caveat-strengthening fix is not yet authored
questions.why_load_bearing: linking-last is a load-bearing sequencing verdict in the make-vs-buy ladder; if it rests only on a downgraded foreign ratio and not on an independent scarcity/skill mechanism, the ordering rule is softer than the spec presents

questions.q: Fresh angle. Your A2 fine-acrylic band ~$3.5-8 is stated as 'the floor' — the cheapest article ex-factory. But the brain's duty inversion (acrylic/MMF ~32% US duty, ~2x cotton's ~16.5%) means A2's factory-gate lead is ERASED at the US border, AND your own inverted-duty/GST drag bites A2 specifically on the India cash-cycle side. So A2 is simultaneously your ex-factory floor and the article most punished the moment it leaves your lane. Without letting the ~32% US duty leak into your ex-factory band (that is T9's), state precisely what you are entitled to SAY to the owner about A2 being 'the floor' — is calling A2 the cheapest article, full stop, a scope-honest ex-factory statement, or does it mislead unless you flag that A2's advantage does not survive the hand-off? What is the smallest honest caveat that must travel with 'A2 is the floor'?
questions.targets: glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' (A2 the floor); boundaries[2] (duty trio excluded, T9); glossary 'inverted-duty / GST drag' (bites A2); conflicts_and_dominance[0]; neutralize_gate N5; dominance_rules landed->unit_economics
questions.failure_mode_probed: a scope-honest but MISLEADING headline — 'A2 is the floor' stated bare invites the owner to read acrylic as the winner, when the same article is the ~2x US-duty outlier AND the GST-inversion victim; the spec may present the floor without the mandatory 'advantage dies at the gate' caveat
questions.why_load_bearing: A2 is the value-driver the whole line leads with; if mfg_economics ships 'A2 is cheapest' without flagging that its lead evaporates at the border and in the refund lag, it hands T9 a number that reads as a recommendation it is not entitled to make

questions.q: Fresh angle on the applied Q1 fix. Round 1's apply_now adds a pointer so that when you DEFER a viability question you carry the DECISION_MEMO GATED-conditional-GO posture. Stress that pointer: an owner shows you the A3 ~$6-22+ band and says 'A3 is expensive to make — so the A3-hero config the memo likes must be the WEAKEST on cost; does that sink the conditional-GO?' Answer while (a) refusing the viability call as not yours, (b) carrying the four-gate framing, and (c) NOT letting your own factory-gate cost read contradict the DECISION_MEMO's A3-hero + bundle-to-AOV logic (where A3's higher ex-factory cost is offset downstream by AOV and margin, not at the loom). Show that 'A3 costs more ex-factory' and 'A3-hero is the one config that closes the math' are NOT in contradiction — and quote the dominance rule that makes viability unit_economics', not yours, so your cost read never overrides the memo.
questions.targets: escalation_triggers[2] (+ the applied Q1 GATED-posture pointer); conflicts_and_dominance[0]; glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' (A3 order-of-magnitude); router dominance viability->unit_economics+DECISION_MEMO; neutralize_gate N7
questions.failure_mode_probed: the applied pointer failing under a case where the specialist's OWN deliverable (A3 is the most expensive article) superficially argues AGAINST the DECISION_MEMO's A3-hero config, tempting a scope-crossing 'A3 is too costly' viability inference that N7 forbids
questions.why_load_bearing: the whole point of the Q1 apply_now is that a deferral still carries the standing verdict; if the specialist's cost read can be turned into an implicit anti-A3 viability argument, the pointer is cosmetic and the dominance rule is not actually protecting unit_economics' lane

questions.q: Fresh angle. Your 'own the iteration loop' carve-out (KB2) lists real equipment bands — used hand-flat ~$200-1,500, used linker ~$500-4,000, used press ~$1,000-8,000 — justified on SPEED/CONTROL, utilisation argument disapplied. Round 1 accepted the speed-axis logic (Q7 ok) but did not test the EQUIPMENT itself. Now probe the build-adjacent edge: a used linker in the sampling cell is the SAME class of machine as the linking bottleneck you say to subcontract and in-source LAST. Reconcile owning a used linker 'for iteration' with the standing linking-last / never-build-a-machine discipline and the machines specialist's authority over linker capacity. At what point does an iteration-cell linker running proven designs become the in-sourced bulk linker you forbade until proven volume — and what bright-line keeps 'own the loop' from becoming 'own linking early through the sampling-cell door'?
questions.targets: KB2 glossary 'own the iteration loop' (equipment bands) + AI_ITERATION_LOOP; conflicts_and_dominance[5]; boundaries[4] (never present a sampling cell as owning bulk); STAGE_LADDER linking=subcontract-LAST; dominance_rules machines-owns-capacity + build=NEVER
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope leak via the equipment list — a used linker owned 'for iteration' is the exact bottleneck machine the ladder says to in-source LAST, so the speed-axis carve-out could authorise owning the scarce linker early, crossing both the linking-last rule and the machines lane, unpoliced by a bright-line
questions.why_load_bearing: the iteration-loop exception is the one place the buy-everything verdict admits owned machines; an unpoliced linker in that cell is precisely the linking-last-and-machines-authority breach the brain guards against, and round 1 did not test the equipment

questions.q: Fresh angle. You warn off a Jul-Oct-peak launch (cluster winter-hosiery peak stretches lead time and working capital) and flag the working-capital trap (~6-12 weeks yarn-in to goods-ready before ocean and sell-through). But your California/Turlock market is WARM — the DECISION_MEMO leads with A3-hero into a climate where heavy knitwear sells fewer months. Reconcile the two seasons that do not align: the Ludhiana SUPPLY peak (Jul-Oct, avoid) versus the California DEMAND window for sweaters. If you must place a bulk order to AVOID the Ludhiana peak yet ARRIVE for the (short) California cool season after ~6-12 weeks conversion plus weeks of ocean, show the calendar actually closes — or concede that 'avoid Jul-Oct' plus the ocean lead plus a warm-market demand window is a scheduling squeeze you name but cannot size, and state whose lane (T7/T9 demand timing) owns the demand half so you do not over-claim a launch date.
questions.targets: KB3 SEASONAL_CASH_TIMING + WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP; glossary 'working-capital trap'; capabilities[4] (Jul-Oct caution); SCOPE_GLOSSARY (warm-California climate); boundaries[2] (P&L/demand is T7/T9)
questions.failure_mode_probed: a one-sided seasonal warning — naming the Ludhiana SUPPLY peak to avoid while silently ignoring that the warm-California DEMAND window is short and on a different calendar, so the working-capital-trap timing advice may be un-closeable or may cross into T7/T9 demand-timing scope
questions.why_load_bearing: the working-capital trap is the modal death (G3); if the specialist's seasonal advice only covers the supply side and hand-waves the demand-arrival calendar, the cash-runway timing it sizes is incomplete at the exact gate the memo calls the modal killer

questions.q: Fresh angle on the compliance-loading arithmetic. You load EPF/ESI ~15%+ 'on the on-roll labour-bearing portion only' (sampling, in-house finishing/QC), NOT the whole stack. In a subcontract-everything launch, the on-roll labour-bearing portion is TINY — most labour sits with job-workers. So quantify honestly: what fraction of a subcontracted A2's ex-factory cost does your ~15%+ EPF/ESI loading actually touch, and is it therefore near-negligible per garment at launch? If it is near-negligible, why does it appear in your cost-stack narrative at all — is it a line that matters only once you OWN the iteration loop / graduate to owning knitting, i.e. a FUTURE cost, not a launch cost? Show you are not overstating a compliance line that, in the buy-everything base case, lands almost entirely on someone else's books (and is therefore inside the [UNKNOWN] rate, per R2Q3).
questions.targets: KB1 EPF_ESI_LOADING + glossary 'compliance loading (EPF/ESI)'; EXFACTORY_BOUNDARY (compliance loading on on-roll portion); capabilities[0].method ('load EPF/ESI on the labour-bearing portion only'); neutralize_gate N1
questions.failure_mode_probed: an over-weighted cost line — presenting EPF/ESI ~15%+ as a stack component when, in the subcontract-everything launch, it touches only a tiny on-roll sliver and the real compliance cost lives inside the [UNKNOWN] job-worker rate; risks double-counting with R2Q3 or implying a launch cost that is actually a future owned-stage cost
questions.why_load_bearing: compliance loading is one of the ten named cost lines; if it materially bites only after graduating to owning stages, presenting it as a base-case launch line either overstates launch cost or blurs the launch-vs-owned boundary the spec claims to police

questions.q: Fresh meta-angle at the decisiveness joint (conflicts_and_dominance[8]). Round 1 confirmed your verdict is falsifiable (Q12) and honest, but EVERY load-bearing number you own — bands, breakeven, first cheque, micro-uplift — is ultimately gated on TWO permanently-held [UNKNOWN]s (the knit+LINK rate and the FOB MOQ) plus a stale single-firm anchor (Vardhman 54%) and a downgraded foreign study (FF-costing). Answer the owner who asks: 'given literally your entire quantitative core is one stale anchor, one downgraded foreign ratio, and two [UNKNOWN]s you refuse to quote, what have you actually DECIDED that a real quote run could not overturn?' Name the conclusions that are RATE-INDEPENDENT and survive any quote outcome (e.g. dyeing never owned, machine never built, dye-lot MOQ is the binding minimum, contribution-after-CAC not factory cost decides viability) versus the ones that are merely PARKED behind the [UNKNOWN]s — and prove you are delivering real decisions, not deferring the entire segment behind blockers.
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[8] (discipline vs decisiveness); NEVER_OWN_DYEHOUSE + NEVER_BUILD_MACHINE (KB2); DYE_LOT_MOQ (KB3); glossary 'two-number frame'; escalation_triggers[0],[1],[6]; validation_checklist
questions.failure_mode_probed: the [UNKNOWN]s and stale anchors used as a blanket shield — a specialist that looks rigorous but has actually PARKED every quantitative conclusion behind blockers, delivering no rate-independent decision; the failure is indecision dressed as honesty discipline
questions.why_load_bearing: the spec's self-claimed virtue is 'labelled-estimate discipline does not excuse indecision'; if it cannot cleanly separate the verdicts that survive any quote from the ones parked behind [UNKNOWN]s, the whole decisive-yet-honest posture collapses into hedging
